alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 1:46AM MDT until October 23 at 4:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Western Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern Hinsdale County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 400 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 146 AM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in
the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
La Plata River, Animas River, Vallecito Creek, Taylor Creek, Los
Pinos River, Florida River, and First Fork Piedra River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Durango, La Plata, Falfa, Hesperus, Bondad, Breen, Mayday, Kline,
Marvel, Redmesa and Vallecito.
- Flooding along the Animas River, including areas on the north
side of Durango, is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Rivers
and streams will continue to rise through the night, with peak
flow expected Friday afternoon.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 11:51PM MDT until October 24 at 12:19AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Colorado...

San Juan River at Pagosa Springs affecting Archuleta County.

For the San Juan River...including Pagosa Springs, Bluff...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...Until late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At 14.5 feet, Water has reached the foundations of some
homes in the San Juan River Ranch northeast of Pagosa Springs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 PM MDT Thursday the stage was 13.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 PM MDT Thursday was 13.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 15.0 feet late tonight. It will
then fall below flood stage tomorrow evening to 8.0 feet Saturday
evening. It will rise to 8.1 feet Sunday morning. It will then
fall again and remain below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 13.5
feet on 06/29/1927.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 9:50PM MDT until October 24 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and Utah,
including the following areas, Arches/Grand Flat,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and
Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...Through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recent burn scars and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Flooding is imminent or ongoing with additional rounds of showers
and thunderstorms expected through Friday afternoon. Rivers and
creeks may still experience high waters even after rainfall has
ended.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 5:44PM MDT until October 23 at 5:45AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 545 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. Several structures are
flooded, and numerous roads remain closed due to flooding impacts
County wide. Streams will likely continue to rise due to excess
runoff and additional rainfall expected overnight.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 528 PM MDT, Public and local law enforcement reported numerous
impacts of flooding occurring across Archuleta County. Between
1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 2 inches are possible in
the warned area this evening and overnight.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Pagosa Springs, Lonetree, Chimney Rock, Juanita, Gato, Pagosa
Junction, Chromo and Arboles.
- The San Juan River continues to rise, and is expected to exceed
Major Flood Stage late this evening and overnight. This flood
warning extends to tributaries, streams, creeks and low-land
areas beyond the San Juan River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 4:37PM MDT until October 23 at 8:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas along
Stollsteimer Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 432 PM MDT, emergency management reported water exceeding
Stollsteimer Creek's banks. Additional rain this evening and
overnight will cause urban and small stream flooding. Between 1
and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Low-lying areas along Stollsteimer Creek.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 11:13AM MDT until October 23 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and river flooding caused by excessive rainfall
is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected, especially along the San
Juan River down to the Navajo River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1107 AM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected in the warned area.
Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen over the last 24
hours. Excess runoff from rainfall will cause the San Juan River
to rise downstream to the Navajo River, potentially inundating
homes.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
San Juan River, Blanco, Rio, Montezuma Creek and Navajo River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Juanita and Gato.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 1:47AM MDT until October 23 at 4:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 400 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding with road washouts also occurring.
Streams and dry washes continue to rise due to excess runoff from
earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 147 AM MDT, local law enforcement reported flooding in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring. Between 1.5 and 2
inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes but is not limited to the following streams
anddrainages...
Florida River, Spring Creek, Ute Creek, Salt Creek and Dry Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Bayfield, Ignacio, Oxford, Tiffany and Allison.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

planned_events.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147600
planned_events.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting October 24, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until October 24, 2026 at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 24, 7:00AM - October 24, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
